title: ORFE T5b - weather hedge venue census
status: complete; page-read pass done 2026-10-02 (21 of 24 page-read lines closed, 3 could not be read); judgement unchanged, reasoning on ForecastEx and Polymarket US changed
question: Does any venue price a 7-day, single-city temperature cover (CHI heat K=90 F, MIA heat K=93 F, NYC cold K=75 F, CHI rain) at under 2x burn in the tails, and list it early enough to hedge cover sold a week or more ahead?
answer: No. Every exchange ladder lists one to two days ahead, none lists a weekly temperature contract, and no venue is shown to price the tail under 2x burn. ForecastEx lists only about nine strikes around the forecast, so it has no tail strikes. Polymarket US has the best station and source match but is a day-ahead two-degree bracket ladder like Kalshi.

judgement_five_lines: No venue prices a 7-day single-city station cover under 2x burn in the tails, and none lists a daily contract more than about two days ahead.
Timing without basis: CME (months ahead, monthly degree days, LaGuardia and O'Hare, no Miami, 20-lot blocks) and the monthly exchange contracts.
Basis without timing: Polymarket US (same source and stations as the covers), Kalshi, and ForecastEx only for Chicago and Miami within about four degrees of the forecast.
Timing and basis together exist only over the counter (Arbol, Descartes, Swiss Re, Munich Re), at minimums of $50K-$100K premium or more.

So the pool carries the week-ahead window itself, uses the cheaper of the Kalshi and Polymarket US brackets once they list, and holds capped tails until the book is big enough to buy an aggregate cover.
